articles.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
articles.summaryTr: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
articles.articleText: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test - Published SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage - at about 1515 local time (2115 GMT) on Saturday. It's the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space. If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? - Published27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test - Published28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

articles.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
articles.summary: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
articles.summaryTr: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
articles.articleText: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans - Published Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told a news conference. There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans. Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort. The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job". Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations. Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

articles.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
articles.summary: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

articles.titleTr: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
articles.summaryTr: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
articles.articleText: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore - Published A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips. Megaspeed is a case in point. It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations. The city-state has had some success in policing this. It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places. They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties. In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore. The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere. Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed. But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department. Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud. In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months. Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case. Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing. In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times. Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses. Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity. On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips. How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness. In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively. For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law. But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities. Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case. BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road. In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed. Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man. During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS. Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences. Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government. All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore. "For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said. Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore". But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips. With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts. Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China. Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said. "Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said. But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China". "This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour." articles.articleText: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı - Türkiye'nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. - Plan kapsamında çalışanların yeni beceriler kazanması, istihdamın korunması ve dönüşümden etkilenen sektör ve bölgelerin desteklenmesi hedefleniyor. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’ın imzasını taşıyan genelge, Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 2027-2029 dönemini kapsayan strateji, iklim değişikliği ile yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün çalışma hayatı üzerindeki etkilerini yönetmeyi amaçlıyor. Genelgede, Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda dönüşüm sürecinin kimseyi geride bırakmadan yürütülmesinin önemine dikkat çekildi. 2 Temmuz 2025 tarihli İklim Kanunu ile mevzuata giren adil geçiş yaklaşımının; çalışanların ve işletmelerin değişen koşullara uyum sağlamasını, yeni beceriler kazanmasını, insana yakışır işlerin artırılmasını ve sosyal korumanın güçlendirilmesini gerektirdiği belirtildi. Üç temel politika ekseni belirlendi Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı koordinasyonunda, ilgili paydaşların katılımıyla hazırlanan strateji üç temel eksene dayanıyor: Beceri uyumu: Çalışanların dönüşen iş gücü piyasasının ihtiyaçlarına uygun beceriler kazanması. Kapsayıcı dönüşüm: Yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün farklı sektör, bölge ve toplumsal gruplar üzerindeki etkilerinin gözetilmesi. Sosyal koruma ve toplumsal dayanıklılık: Dönüşüm sürecinde çalışanların ve toplumun desteklenmesi. Plan kapsamında öncelikli sektörlere yönelik sektörel politikalar da uygulanacak. Uygulama altı ayda bir raporlanacak Strateji ve Eylem Planı, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı'nın resmi internet sitesinde yayımlanacak. Planın koordinasyon, izleme ve değerlendirme çalışmaları ilgili kamu kurumları ve sosyal tarafların katılımıyla Bakanlık tarafından yürütülecek. Eylem Planı'nda sorumlu olarak belirlenen kurum ve kuruluşlar, uygulamadaki gelişmeleri altı aylık dönemler halinde Bakanlığa bildirecek. Adil geçiş, düşük karbonlu ve çevre dostu ekonomiye geçiş sırasında çalışanların, işletmelerin ve bölgelerin olumsuz etkilenmesini önlemeyi amaçlayan politika yaklaşımıdır. Temel hedef, yeşil dönüşümün istihdam ve sosyal haklar üzerindeki maliyetlerini azaltırken yeni iş ve beceri fırsatları yaratmaktır.

articles.articleText: Sözleşmeli personele yeni dönem! Disiplin cezalarından izinlere birçok kural değişti - Kamuda 4/B statüsünde görev yapan sözleşmeli personeli ilgilendiren yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. - Disiplin cezalarından hastalık izinlerine, göreve başlama sürelerinden kurum içi yer değişikliklerine kadar birçok konuda yeni kurallar getirildi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın imzasıyla yayımlanan 11982 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanı Kararı, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yürürlüğe girdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 657 sayılı Devlet Memurları Kanunu'nun 4/B maddesi kapsamında çalışan sözleşmeli personelin çalışma koşullarını düzenleyen kararla mevcut esaslarda değişiklik yapıldı. Sözleşmeli personele disiplin cezaları uygulanacak Yeni düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin disipline aykırı fiil ve davranışlarında devlet memurlarına uygulanan disiplin hükümlerinin kıyasen uygulanması kararlaştırıldı. Buna göre disiplin cezalarının belirlenmesi, yetkili merciler ve disiplin kurullarının işleyişinde memurlara ilişkin hükümler esas alınacak. Aylıktan kesme cezası ise personelin pozisyonuna bağlı ödemelerin toplamı üzerinden 1/30 ile 1/8 arasında uygulanabilecek. Kademe ilerlemesinin durdurulması ve daha ağır cezaları gerektiren fiillerde disiplin kurulu kararı alınacak. Personelin görevine, atamaya yetkili amirin onayıyla son verilebilecek. Hastalık izinleri ve rapor süreleri değişti Hastalık ve refakat izinlerinde, 657 sayılı Kanun'un 105'inci maddesindeki ilgili hükümler sözleşmeli personele de uygulanacak. SGK tarafından ödenen geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği ise personelin ücretinden düşülecek. Azami hastalık izni süresinin tamamlanmasının ardından göreve başlanmaması da sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine ilişkin hükümler arasına eklendi. Göreve başlama sürelerine sınır getirildi Yeni kurallara göre aynı yerde göreve başlayacak personelin, tebliği izleyen iş günü içinde işe başlaması gerekecek. Başka bir yerde görevlendirilen personel ise tebliğ tarihinden itibaren 15 günü izleyen iş günü içinde görevine başlayacak. Belgeyle ispatlanabilen zorlayıcı nedenler dışında bu sürelere uyulmaması, sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine neden olabilecek. Kurum içi yer değişikliğinde 3 yıl şartı 4/B kapsamında çalışan personelin kurum içi yer değişiklikleri de yeniden düzenlendi. Buna göre personelin işe başladığı tarihten itibaren aynı kurumda üç yıllık çalışma süresini tamamlayana kadar yapacağı yer değişikliklerinde belirlenen özel usul ve esaslar uygulanacak. Sözleşmeli personelin görevden uzaklaştırılmasında da devlet memurlarına ilişkin hükümler kıyasen geçerli olacak. Memur kadrosuna geçenlerin boş pozisyonları iptal edilecek Sözleşmeli personelin memur kadrosuna atanması halinde boşalan sözleşmeli personel pozisyonları, başka bir işleme gerek kalmaksızın iptal edilmiş sayılacak. İptal edilen pozisyonlar ilgili kamu personel bilgi sistemine bildirilecek. Eğitim ve ücret ödemelerinde yeni hükümler Düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin temel eğitim, hazırlayıcı eğitim ve staj süreçlerinin görev yaptıkları kurumlar tarafından yürütülmesi kararlaştırıldı. Hizmet içi eğitimlerle personelin mesleki gelişiminin desteklenmesi de öngörüldü. Ücretlerin ay başında peşin ödenmesi uygulaması devam edecek. Ancak ay sonundan önce görevden ayrılan personelden kalan günlere ilişkin ödemeler geri alınacak. Memur kadrosuna atananlar, kendisine aylık bağlananlar ve hayatını kaybeden personel bu uygulamanın dışında tutulacak. Yeni düzenleme, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanmasıyla yürürlüğe girdi.

Disiplin cezalarından izinlere birçok kural değişti - Kamuda 4/B statüsünde görev yapan sözleşmeli personeli ilgilendiren yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. - Disiplin cezalarından hastalık izinlerine, göreve başlama sürelerinden kurum içi yer değişikliklerine kadar birçok konuda yeni kurallar getirildi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın imzasıyla yayımlanan 11982 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanı Kararı, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yürürlüğe girdi. articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake, and Trump nominated four SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for Hester Peirce. OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said. The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction. The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%. The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings. Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million. Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday. The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million). Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

articles.summaryTr: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek.
articles.articleText: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. - İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. SPK bülteninde yer alan karara göre Plastikkart Akıllı Kart İletişim Sistemleri'nin 22 milyon 750 bin TL olan mevcut sermayesi, 277 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 300 milyon TL’ye çıkarılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Flap Kongre Toplantı Hizmetleri'nin ise 93 milyon 750 bin TL olan sermayesi, 306 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 400 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. Böylece iki şirketin sermaye artırımına konu toplam bedelsiz tutarı 583 milyon 500 bin TL olacak. Bedelsiz sermaye artırımı, şirketlerin iç kaynaklarını (yedek akçeler, geçmiş yıl kârları veya sermaye düzeltmesi olumlu farkları gibi) kullanarak sermayelerini artırmasıdır. Bu işlemde yatırımcılar yeni payları ücretsiz alır; hisse sayısı artarken yatırımcının şirketteki ortaklık oranı, diğer koşullar aynı kaldığı sürece değişmez. Hisse fiyatı ise sermaye artırımına bağlı olarak teorik biçimde düzeltilir.

articles.articleText: SPK'dan tasfiye edilen fonların iadesine ilişkin yeni karar: Şirketlere açıklama zorunluluğu YAYIN TARİHİ, 14 Kasım 2026 00:17 GÜNCELLEME, 14 Kasım 2026 01:18 PAYLAŞ - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. - Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu. SPK, tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarından elde edilen kazançların halka açık şirketler tarafından isteğe bağlı olarak iade edilmesine ilişkin esasları belirledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İadelerin hisse fiyatını veya yatırımcı kararlarını etkileyebilecek nitelikte olması halinde özel durum açıklaması yapılacak. Kurulun duyurduğu ilkelere göre şirketler, söz konusu iade ödemelerini genel kurul toplantılarında ayrı bir gündem maddesiyle pay sahiplerinin bilgisine sunacak. Ödemelerin finansal tablolara nasıl yansıtılacağı ve dipnotlarda nasıl açıklanacağı ise Türkiye Muhasebe ve Finansal Raporlama Standartları çerçevesinde değerlendirilecek.

articles.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
articles.summary: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
articles.summaryTr: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
articles.articleText: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption - Published Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. - Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published5 hours ago - Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world - Published6 hours ago In the UK, some parts of the NHS, including GPs and hospitals, were affected, as were some schools and police forces. UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls, and there had been no disruption to the transport network. In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails. In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook. Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday. In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook. The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals. Peter Pentz, a winemaker in South Africa, said his entire business was basically brought to a "standstill". His winery's communication with exports was also brought to a standstill, he said, and "critical production work" was been halted as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations". Georgia from Staffordshire in England said she was due to complete her first house purchase today after waiting eight months to get to this point - but the outage has delayed that. "The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies. "We're not the only one completing today, there are hundreds of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible," Georgia said. 'Encouraging recovery signals' Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally. While it launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world. By 13:32, the tech giant said there were "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region. Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remain stable once they are up and running again. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously." Microsoft said it has no "ETA" for when services will be fully recovered. A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review. Experts said while workers may have been happy to not have email access for the day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services. "The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure. Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem. "Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said. "In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur." articles.title: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9325-26 CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced that it has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state’s attempts to halt event-contract trading and impose up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement against Kalshi in state court, a CFTC-designated contract market. Arkansas’s efforts to obstruct the functions of CFTC-registered exchanges operating lawfully under the Commodity Exchange Act are preempted by federal law. “As prediction markets continue to prove their value in being useful for risk management and providing the public with valuable information about the future, Arkansas seeks to shut down event contracts ranging from sports and politics to other important world events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act, and the Commission will not let state interference thwart its regulatory efforts and destroy federally regulated markets.” Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued to vindicate federal sovereign interests. The CFTC has also submitted amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court. -CFTC-

news.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
news.summaryTr: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
news.articleText: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test - Published SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage - at about 1515 local time (2115 GMT) on Saturday. It's the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space. If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? - Published27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test - Published28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space. If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? - Published27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test - Published28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

news.titleTr: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
news.summaryTr: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
news.articleText: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans - Published Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told a news conference. There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans. Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort. The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job". Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations. Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

news.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
news.summary: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

news.titleTr: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
news.summaryTr: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
news.articleText: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore - Published A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips. Megaspeed is a case in point. It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations. The city-state has had some success in policing this. It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places. They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties. In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore. The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere. Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed. But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department. Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud. In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months. Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case. Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing. In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times. Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses. Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity. On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips. How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness. In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively. For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law. But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities. Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case. BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road. In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed. Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man. During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS. Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences. Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government. All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore. "For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said. Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore". But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips. With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts. Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China. Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said. "Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said. But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China". "This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour." Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit. - Published21 hours ago - Published1 day ago

news.titleTr: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı
news.summaryTr: Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. news.articleText: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı - Türkiye'nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. - Plan kapsamında çalışanların yeni beceriler kazanması, istihdamın korunması ve dönüşümden etkilenen sektör ve bölgelerin desteklenmesi hedefleniyor. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’ın imzasını taşıyan genelge, Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 2027-2029 dönemini kapsayan strateji, iklim değişikliği ile yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün çalışma hayatı üzerindeki etkilerini yönetmeyi amaçlıyor. Genelgede, Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda dönüşüm sürecinin kimseyi geride bırakmadan yürütülmesinin önemine dikkat çekildi. 2 Temmuz 2025 tarihli İklim Kanunu ile mevzuata giren adil geçiş yaklaşımının; çalışanların ve işletmelerin değişen koşullara uyum sağlamasını, yeni beceriler kazanmasını, insana yakışır işlerin artırılmasını ve sosyal korumanın güçlendirilmesini gerektirdiği belirtildi. Üç temel politika ekseni belirlendi Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı koordinasyonunda, ilgili paydaşların katılımıyla hazırlanan strateji üç temel eksene dayanıyor: Beceri uyumu: Çalışanların dönüşen iş gücü piyasasının ihtiyaçlarına uygun beceriler kazanması. Kapsayıcı dönüşüm: Yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün farklı sektör, bölge ve toplumsal gruplar üzerindeki etkilerinin gözetilmesi. Sosyal koruma ve toplumsal dayanıklılık: Dönüşüm sürecinde çalışanların ve toplumun desteklenmesi. Plan kapsamında öncelikli sektörlere yönelik sektörel politikalar da uygulanacak. Uygulama altı ayda bir raporlanacak Strateji ve Eylem Planı, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı'nın resmi internet sitesinde yayımlanacak. Planın koordinasyon, izleme ve değerlendirme çalışmaları ilgili kamu kurumları ve sosyal tarafların katılımıyla Bakanlık tarafından yürütülecek. Eylem Planı'nda sorumlu olarak belirlenen kurum ve kuruluşlar, uygulamadaki gelişmeleri altı aylık dönemler halinde Bakanlığa bildirecek. Adil geçiş, düşük karbonlu ve çevre dostu ekonomiye geçiş sırasında çalışanların, işletmelerin ve bölgelerin olumsuz etkilenmesini önlemeyi amaçlayan politika yaklaşımıdır. Temel hedef, yeşil dönüşümün istihdam ve sosyal haklar üzerindeki maliyetlerini azaltırken yeni iş ve beceri fırsatları yaratmaktır.

news.titleTr: Sözleşmeli personele yeni dönem! Disiplin cezalarından izinlere birçok kural değişti
news.summaryTr: Kamuda 4/B statüsünde görev yapan sözleşmeli personeli ilgilendiren yeni düzenleme Resmî Gazete’de yayımlandı. Disiplin cezalarından hastalık izinlerine, göreve başlama sürelerinden kurum içi yer değişikliklerine kadar birçok konuda yeni kurallar getirildi.
news.articleText: Sözleşmeli personele yeni dönem! Disiplin cezalarından izinlere birçok kural değişti - Kamuda 4/B statüsünde görev yapan sözleşmeli personeli ilgilendiren yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. - Disiplin cezalarından hastalık izinlerine, göreve başlama sürelerinden kurum içi yer değişikliklerine kadar birçok konuda yeni kurallar getirildi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın imzasıyla yayımlanan 11982 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanı Kararı, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yürürlüğe girdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 657 sayılı Devlet Memurları Kanunu'nun 4/B maddesi kapsamında çalışan sözleşmeli personelin çalışma koşullarını düzenleyen kararla mevcut esaslarda değişiklik yapıldı. Sözleşmeli personele disiplin cezaları uygulanacak Yeni düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin disipline aykırı fiil ve davranışlarında devlet memurlarına uygulanan disiplin hükümlerinin kıyasen uygulanması kararlaştırıldı. Buna göre disiplin cezalarının belirlenmesi, yetkili merciler ve disiplin kurullarının işleyişinde memurlara ilişkin hükümler esas alınacak. Aylıktan kesme cezası ise personelin pozisyonuna bağlı ödemelerin toplamı üzerinden 1/30 ile 1/8 arasında uygulanabilecek. Kademe ilerlemesinin durdurulması ve daha ağır cezaları gerektiren fiillerde disiplin kurulu kararı alınacak. Personelin görevine, atamaya yetkili amirin onayıyla son verilebilecek. Hastalık izinleri ve rapor süreleri değişti Hastalık ve refakat izinlerinde, 657 sayılı Kanun'un 105'inci maddesindeki ilgili hükümler sözleşmeli personele de uygulanacak. SGK tarafından ödenen geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği ise personelin ücretinden düşülecek. Azami hastalık izni süresinin tamamlanmasının ardından göreve başlanmaması da sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine ilişkin hükümler arasına eklendi. Göreve başlama sürelerine sınır getirildi Yeni kurallara göre aynı yerde göreve başlayacak personelin, tebliği izleyen iş günü içinde işe başlaması gerekecek. Başka bir yerde görevlendirilen personel ise tebliğ tarihinden itibaren 15 günü izleyen iş günü içinde görevine başlayacak. Belgeyle ispatlanabilen zorlayıcı nedenler dışında bu sürelere uyulmaması, sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine neden olabilecek. Kurum içi yer değişikliğinde 3 yıl şartı 4/B kapsamında çalışan personelin kurum içi yer değişiklikleri de yeniden düzenlendi. Buna göre personelin işe başladığı tarihten itibaren aynı kurumda üç yıllık çalışma süresini tamamlayana kadar yapacağı yer değişikliklerinde belirlenen özel usul ve esaslar uygulanacak. Sözleşmeli personelin görevden uzaklaştırılmasında da devlet memurlarına ilişkin hükümler kıyasen geçerli olacak. Memur kadrosuna geçenlerin boş pozisyonları iptal edilecek Sözleşmeli personelin memur kadrosuna atanması halinde boşalan sözleşmeli personel pozisyonları, başka bir işleme gerek kalmaksızın iptal edilmiş sayılacak. İptal edilen pozisyonlar ilgili kamu personel bilgi sistemine bildirilecek. Eğitim ve ücret ödemelerinde yeni hükümler Düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin temel eğitim, hazırlayıcı eğitim ve staj süreçlerinin görev yaptıkları kurumlar tarafından yürütülmesi kararlaştırıldı. Hizmet içi eğitimlerle personelin mesleki gelişiminin desteklenmesi de öngörüldü. Ücretlerin ay başında peşin ödenmesi uygulaması devam edecek. Ancak ay sonundan önce görevden ayrılan personelden kalan günlere ilişkin ödemeler geri alınacak. Memur kadrosuna atananlar, kendisine aylık bağlananlar ve hayatını kaybeden personel bu uygulamanın dışında tutulacak. Yeni düzenleme, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanmasıyla yürürlüğe girdi.

news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake, and Trump nominated four SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for Hester Peirce. OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said. The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction. The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%. The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings. Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million. Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday. The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million). Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. news.titleTr: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı
news.summaryTr: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek.
news.articleText: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. - İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. SPK bülteninde yer alan karara göre Plastikkart Akıllı Kart İletişim Sistemleri'nin 22 milyon 750 bin TL olan mevcut sermayesi, 277 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 300 milyon TL’ye çıkarılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Flap Kongre Toplantı Hizmetleri'nin ise 93 milyon 750 bin TL olan sermayesi, 306 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 400 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. Böylece iki şirketin sermaye artırımına konu toplam bedelsiz tutarı 583 milyon 500 bin TL olacak. Bedelsiz sermaye artırımı, şirketlerin iç kaynaklarını (yedek akçeler, geçmiş yıl kârları veya sermaye düzeltmesi olumlu farkları gibi) kullanarak sermayelerini artırmasıdır. Bu işlemde yatırımcılar yeni payları ücretsiz alır; hisse sayısı artarken yatırımcının şirketteki ortaklık oranı, diğer koşullar aynı kaldığı sürece değişmez. Hisse fiyatı ise sermaye artırımına bağlı olarak teorik biçimde düzeltilir.

Havada bulunan uçakların inişine izin verilirken yerdeki uçakların yeni bir duyuruya kadar kalkış yapamayacağı bildirildi.
news.articleText: ABD'de tüm uçuşlar durduruldu! FAA'dan ülke genelinde kalkış yasağı - ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), hava trafik kontrol iletişim sistemlerinde yaşanan ciddi sorunların ardından güvenlik gerekçesiyle ülke genelindeki tüm kalkışları durdurdu. - Havada bulunan uçakların inişine izin verilirken yerdeki uçakların yeni bir duyuruya kadar kalkış yapamayacağı bildirildi. FAA, cuma günü yaptığı açıklamada, olağanüstü koşullar ve güvenlik gerekçeleri nedeniyle ülke genelinde kalkışlara yönelik yer durdurma kararı alındığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Açıklama öncesinde Chicago'daki hava trafiği de iletişim sorunları nedeniyle durduruldu. Uluslararası uçuşların ise vaka bazında değerlendirileceği belirtildi. Karar, havadaki uçakların inişini engellemiyor ancak yerde bekleyen uçakların kalkış yapmasına izin vermiyor. 11 Eylül'den bu yana ikinci kez Ülke genelindeki tüm kalkışların durdurulması, 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ikinci kez yaşandı. Daha önce Ocak 2023'te FAA, sistemdeki bir sorun nedeniyle ABD'deki tüm iç hat kalkışlarını iki saatten kısa süreyle durdurmuştu. FAA için 30,1 milyar dolarlık ek kaynak talebi ABD Kongresi, geçen yıl FAA'nın eskiyen iletişim sistemlerinin yenilenmesi için 12,5 milyar dolarlık bütçeyi onaylamıştı. FAA ve Beyaz Saray ise cuma günü diğer sorunların giderilmesi amacıyla Kongre'den ilave 30,1 milyar dolar talep etti. FAA, ABD'de sivil havacılığın güvenliğini ve hava trafik yönetimini düzenleyen federal kurum olarak görev yapıyor. Karar, hava trafik kontrolündeki iletişim altyapısının uçuş güvenliği açısından önemini yeniden gündeme taşıdı.

news.summary: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu.

news.titleTr: SPK'dan tasfiye edilen fonların iadesine ilişkin yeni karar: Şirketlere açıklama zorunluluğu

news.articleText: SPK'dan tasfiye edilen fonların iadesine ilişkin yeni karar: Şirketlere açıklama zorunluluğu YAYIN TARİHİ, 14 Kasım 2026 00:17 GÜNCELLEME, 14 Kasım 2026 01:18 PAYLAŞ - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. - Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu. SPK, tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarından elde edilen kazançların halka açık şirketler tarafından isteğe bağlı olarak iade edilmesine ilişkin esasları belirledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İadelerin hisse fiyatını veya yatırımcı kararlarını etkileyebilecek nitelikte olması halinde özel durum açıklaması yapılacak. Kurulun duyurduğu ilkelere göre şirketler, söz konusu iade ödemelerini genel kurul toplantılarında ayrı bir gündem maddesiyle pay sahiplerinin bilgisine sunacak. Ödemelerin finansal tablolara nasıl yansıtılacağı ve dipnotlarda nasıl açıklanacağı ise Türkiye Muhasebe ve Finansal Raporlama Standartları çerçevesinde değerlendirilecek.

news.articleText: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans A cargo ship has collided with a docked cruise ship in New Orleans, Louisiana, with reports suggesting more than 120 people were on board the cruise ship. Eyewitness video shows the moment the cruise ship is seen sinking and the aftermath of the collision as rescue efforts are under way. New Orleans mayor Helena Moreno has said all passengers have been accounted for.

news.titleTr: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
news.summaryTr: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
news.articleText: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption - Published Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. - Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published5 hours ago - Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world - Published6 hours ago In the UK, some parts of the NHS, including GPs and hospitals, were affected, as were some schools and police forces. UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls, and there had been no disruption to the transport network. In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails. In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook. Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday. In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook. The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals. Peter Pentz, a winemaker in South Africa, said his entire business was basically brought to a "standstill". His winery's communication with exports was also brought to a standstill, he said, and "critical production work" was been halted as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations". Georgia from Staffordshire in England said she was due to complete her first house purchase today after waiting eight months to get to this point - but the outage has delayed that. "The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies. "We're not the only one completing today, there are hundreds of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible," Georgia said. 'Encouraging recovery signals' Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally. While it launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world. By 13:32, the tech giant said there were "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region. Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remain stable once they are up and running again. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously." Microsoft said it has no "ETA" for when services will be fully recovered. A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review. Experts said while workers may have been happy to not have email access for the day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services. "The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure. Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem. "Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said. "In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur." news.summary: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), kredili sermaye piyasası işlemlerinde özkaynak oranının esnetilerek uygulanmasına yönelik tedbirin 31 Aralık 2026 seans sonuna kadar devam etmesine karar verdi.
